evals.expected_output: A full pass: state diff, inventory, shipped tooling work, update-tooling refresh, machine upgrades including claude update and claude doctor, background-process audit, latency numbers, config audit, a verdict-first report, a questionnaire, and a recorded state file.
expectations: Runs checkup_state.py diff, inventory.sh, and claude doctor through pty_capture.py before changing anything
Follows the update-tooling skill for the repository refresh instead of re-implementing it
Runs dotfiles-upgrade (Topgrade) and claude update, and verifies claude --version after the update
Runs background_audit.sh and echo_latency.py and reports their numbers
Runs audit_agent_config.py and reports errors with the repository that owns each fix
Writes the report with the verdict first and separate stability and feature lists
Asks the questionnaire with AskUserQuestion and records the run with checkup_state.py record

evals.prompt: /tooling-checkup — and finish all outstanding PRs while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: Ships the user's and agents' tooling pull requests, but treats dependabot pull requests as not outstanding unless a critical alert is open.
expectations: Does not merge, rebase, or fix a dependabot pull request that the user did not name
Reports dependabot pull requests as one skip line with a count
Fixes an open critical dependabot alert and ships the fix with /ship-it
Reports high alerts as a one-line summary without acting on them
Reports automation branches (bot verdict) as a count, not as outstanding work

evals.prompt: /tooling-checkup. Note: I have another app under ~/apps with a dirty feature branch and three worktrees.
evals.expected_output: Leaves every repository outside the tooling root untouched and does not list it as outstanding work.
expectations: Inventories only primary checkouts directly under TOOLING_ROOT
Does not fetch, commit, push, or clean up the repository outside the tooling root
Does not mention that repository's branches in the Shipped or Needs you sections

evals.prompt: /tooling-checkup (the last run was 20 hours ago and nothing has changed since).
evals.expected_output: A short repeat run that uses the fast paths and says nothing changed.
expectations: Reads the state diff and reports that no versions or repository heads changed
Skips the long dotfiles-upgrade run only when the last upgrade is under 12 hours old and brew has nothing outdated; otherwise runs it
Replays the cached config audit when no input file changed
Still runs the live checks: inventory, update-tooling health checks, background audit, and latency
Records the new run at the end

evals.prompt: Clean up my background processes. There is a Steam cleaner job, a duplicate com.dotfiles job, and a LaunchAgent whose program no longer exists.
evals.expected_output: Tooling-owned problems are fixed in their source repository; third-party removals are asked first and done by moving the plist.
expectations: Runs background_audit.sh and quotes the verdicts
Fixes the duplicate com.dotfiles job in the dotfiles source, not by editing the installed plist
Asks the user before disabling the third-party jobs
Disables an approved job with launchctl bootout and moves its plist to the tooling-checkup state directory instead of deleting it
Gives the user sudo commands for jobs under /Library instead of running them

evals.prompt: Typing in Claude Code in Ghostty feels laggy. Make it faster.
evals.expected_output: Measured before and after numbers, the main cause named, and only safe reversible changes.
expectations: Measures zsh -f and claude with echo_latency.py three times before any change
Counts open Claude Code sessions and checks load, ~/.claude.json size, and orphaned temp files
Moves orphaned ~/.claude.json.tmp files instead of deleting them
Does not claim an improvement without after numbers that beat the run-to-run spread
Does not recommend --bare, --strict-mcp-config, or renderer toggles without new numbers

evals.prompt: Check that all my skills, rules, and AGENTS.md files follow Claude's best practices.
evals.expected_output: Script findings plus judgment checks, with each fix made in the source that owns it.
expectations: Fetches the current Anthropic skills, best-practices, and memory docs
Runs audit_agent_config.py and groups findings by owning repository
Fixes a repeated line in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md at its agentbrew source, not in the generated file
Reports third-party installed skills without editing them
Ships small fixes with /ship-it and puts large changes such as splitting a long AGENTS.md in the questionnaire

evals.prompt: /tooling-checkup. claude doctor says the last update attempt failed.
evals.expected_output: Claude Code is updated and verified, and the failed attempt is reported with evidence.
expectations: Captures claude doctor output with pty_capture.py
Runs claude update and compares claude --version before and after
Reports the doctor line that is not OK in the Updated section
Says that running sessions keep the old binary until restarted
